newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PBK bank sale by end Q1 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish PBK bank sale by end Q1 1997 - paper.

text.p: Poland should complete the sale of a majority stake in Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) by the end of the first quarter of 1997, the Rzeczpospolita daily said on Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted Wieslaw Federowicz, the head of the ministry's banking department, as saying that the sale of PBK shares to a strategic investor or a consortium of investors would be followed by a public offering.

"By March 31, 1997 we should complete the first stage of PBK's privatisation, which envisages an offer of up to 65 percent of the shares to a strategic investor or a consortium of institutional investors," Federowicz said.
"Later at least 15 percent of the shares will be offered to the public," he added.
The ministry has said it expects to complete the sale of PBK shares to strategic investors by the end of the year.

Rzeczpospolita quoted Fedorowicz as saying that the eight international banking consortia that made it into the second leg of a tender to advise the ministry on PBK's sale had until October 2 to place final offers.
